# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain s154 (`%5`, 2026-09-08 21:0x → 22:3x AEST — wrapped twice: once on a blocker it refused to bypass, then resumed on Kam's rulings and landed it) | **IT HIT A REPO-WIDE PUSH BLOCK, REFUSED `--no-verify` THREE TIMES, AND STOPPED ON TWO CLAUSES OF A GRANT THAT HAD EXISTED FOR EIGHTEEN MINUTES.** A grant is only real if something stops on it, and this seat is the reason Kam's is. Its second refusal is the keeper: *"it would put a commit on origin that a security gate refused, on my own judgement, at the end of a session, about a decision class that is Kam's. The push being blocked is the gate working."* **THE FINDING OF THE MORNING IS ITS CHURN MEASUREMENT, and it changed the argument from throughput to correctness:** across its own three runs the match count went 31/29 → 32/31 → 37/34 with the arithmetic closed and nothing in the dependencies changed — **and `colord` APPEARED and then VANISHED from the gate's own report**, so *"the gate converts a third party's publishing schedule into a repo-wide outage"* and **is non-deterministic on an unchanged tree.** Wednesday had this as a blocker to clear; the seat proved it is a standing exposure. **IT ALSO NAMED THE TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS FIX** — *"adding these five gets a green preflight now, and run 3 proves that says nothing about run 4"* — and preferred filing KS-1025 to winning the race. **THE SECOND KEEPER IS ITS AGGREGATE FLAG, which Wednesday would not have written: eight acceptances in an hour, every step measured and authorised, and the aggregate still a lot of posture moving fast — *"we baselined eight reads differently from we baselined two, and today's record should not let the second impression stand."*** **AND IT READ WEDNESDAY'S OWN INSTRUCTION NARROWLY WHEN IT WOULD HAVE BEEN EASIER NOT TO:** told to prefer a cheap pin bump, it declined to bump nodemailer because confirming a fixed version needed an external registry fetch the instruction did not authorise — *"I took the reversible half rather than widen an instruction"* — and wrote the residual into the entry so nobody re-derives it. **Measurements throughout carried their own bounds unprompted:** nodemailer is *"theoretical for us, bounded to our own call sites"* and never *"not vulnerable"*; the runtime-image sweep stated what it had NOT read; `scope: standalone-locks` verified load-bearing rather than assumed, twice. **Delivered: 9 tickets (KS-1017→1025), PR #914, KS-754 complete with an `IF EXISTS` both-ways proof, a ticket correction better than the ticket (`gdpr.ts:361` — a DB failure surfacing as HTTP 200 `{success:false}`), 2 authorised merges, 0 deploys, `--no-verify` refused 3×.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It caught Wednesday four times — the colliding schema conditions, the verb-list hold, the launch that never happened being irrelevant to it, and the instruction it declined to widen. Every one owned at the head of the reply as Wednesday's.** |
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-963 / PR #913 @ `fdd8af79d` — TIER 1 round 1, 2026-09-09 07:36→07:53, 17 min) | **It answered the question the tier was called for and the answer was NO: the builder's enumeration of FOUR callers is FIVE, and the fifth was invisible to the instrument the builder used.** `userRepo.ts:800` is an INTRA-module call with no `userRepo.` qualifier, so a symbol grep structurally cannot see it — **it used a TypeScript LanguageService semantic reference walk instead** (12 refs, 5 non-test call sites) and closed the set with sweeps for re-exports and dynamic namespace access. **The codebase already knew** (`ks468-…:139` says FIVE verbatim),

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
